castor.headlineHtml: Stop Hand-Labeling Training Folders. Gemini Now Governs Drive in Plain English.
castor.standfirstHtml: Yesterday, Google connected shareable Gemini Skills directly to live Google Drive files. Today, on November 17, 2026, Google Workspace shipped the missing security counterpart: Gemini-powered data classification in Google Drive is now Generally Available.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google Workspace elevated Gemini-powered AI data classification in Google Drive to GA (extended rollout Nov 17 – Dec 15, 2026), adding pre-deploy "Test your instructions" previews and near real-time reporting.

Security teams no longer spend weeks tagging manual sample sets to train a custom ML classifier—plain-English Admin console instructions classify Shared Drives and prevent autonomous agents from touching unlabeled secrets.

Organizations get 1 active Gemini instruction model (out of 5 AI models total), files need at least 50 words and 200 characters of readable/OCR text, and instruction edits do not trigger on-demand rescans of already-evaluated files.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · HUMAN, ADMIN & ENTERPRISE GOVERNANCE LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Data Hygiene Is the Prerequisite for Safe Enterprise Agents
castor.subtitleHtml: How replacing manual ML sample training with natural-language Drive instructions closes the agentic leakage gap.
paragraphsHtml: Every company deploying AI assistants eventually hits the same wall: regex Data Loss Prevention (DLP) catches credit card numbers and tax IDs, yet misses the sensitive context inside an unformatted acquisition memo, customer pricing sheet, or internal outage postmortem.

Previously, teaching Google Drive AI classification to recognize those documents meant gathering balanced training folders, manually labeling dozens of representative files per tier, and waiting for a custom machine learning model to stabilize. On November 17, 2026, Google Workspace made Gemini-powered data classification in Google Drive Generally Available, eliminating manual model training in favor of administrator-defined natural-language instructions.

Crucially, Google explicitly ties this GA launch to the agentic era: once files are labeled accurately across Shared Drives and licensed My Drives, DLP policies, retention rules, and Connected App boundaries can automatically keep autonomous workflows from accessing or acting on confidential records.

To give cautious security teams confidence before flipping auto-apply across millions of files, GA introduces two safeguards: a Test your instructions preview right inside the Admin console, plus near real-time reporting tracking labeled file counts, employee label acceptance rates, and Drive inventory.

pullquote.quoteHtml: You cannot safely give autonomous agents live access to company folders until classification runs at the speed of plain English—and respects every human override.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Will Gemini overwrite labels our employees or DLP rules already applied?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: No. Google guarantees Gemini classification will not overwrite labels manually applied, accepted, or modified by users, nor labels applied by DLP rules—and every auto-label, acceptance, and edit is captured in Workspace Audit Logs.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Does Gemini Drive classification respect US and EU Data Regions?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Yes. Eligible Drive content is processed and stored within your designated Google Workspace Data Region (US or Europe) based on file owner or Shared Drive policy, and your files and prompts are never used to train Google’s global models.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: What files are skipped or excluded from evaluation?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Client-side encrypted (CSE) files, non-text media without readable text, and brief notes below ~50 words and 200 characters of readable or OCR-extracted text are skipped.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · WORKSPACE ARCHITECTURE & POLICY LENS
pollux.titleHtml: Designing Your 1-Model Instruction Set, Backfill Queue & DLP Gate
pollux.subtitleHtml: How to structure single-select labels, honor the 50-word threshold, and test policies in the Admin console.
paragraphsHtml: Under the hood, organizations are allocated 1 active Gemini instruction model within a ceiling of 5 total AI classification models (combining custom-trained ML models and Gemini instructions). Labels must target a published single-select options list or badge list field.

When an admin enables auto-apply, Workspace launches a one-time background backfill across existing and inactive files (typically starting within 1 to 2 weeks and completing over weeks or months depending on repository scale). Updating instructions afterward applies to future uploads and modified content—on-demand rescanning of already evaluated files is not included in this release.

Because Gemini evaluates both native text and OCR-extracted text inside PDFs and images once a file crosses 50 words and 200 characters, teams should pair semantic Gemini labels with deterministic regex DLP rules for short code snippets or CSE vaults.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Consolidate Into One Clean Sensitivity Taxonomy
builderRules.detailHtml: Use your 1 active Gemini instruction model with a single-select badge field (e.g., Restricted, Confidential, Internal, Public) so every department shares consistent DLP triggers.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Always Run "Test Your Instructions" Before Auto-Apply
builderRules.detailHtml: Preview candidate files in the Admin console first—since editing instructions later does not trigger an on-demand rescan of already-evaluated files.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Wire Agent Exclusion Rules to the Resulting Labels
builderRules.detailHtml: Configure DLP external-sharing blocks and Gemini Skill / RAG exclusion policies around Confidential and Restricted badges while keeping CSE vaults under strict folder IAM.

mebsuta.headlineHtml: A Robot in a Box to a Working Conveyor in an Afternoon. Inside Hydrogen Robotics.
mebsuta.standfirstHtml: For years, building a physical AI application meant weeks of driver glue, camera calibration scripts, and disconnected simulators before a single grasp ran. On November 17, 2026, Google DeepMind’s Gemini Robotics team paired Gemini 4 Hydrogen’s embodied spatial reasoning with the new Robotics plugin for Google Antigravity.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google launched the Robotics plugin for Google Antigravity (Build With Google shelf) alongside Gemini 4 Hydrogen’s embodied benchmarks: 58 on Artificial Analysis Robotics 0.1 and ERQA leadership over Gemini Robotics ER 2.

Developers can plug an I2RT YAM, SO-ARM101, or FR3 Duo into a laptop via USB, calibrate in ~10 minutes, validate grasps in embedded MuJoCo "vibe sim", and deploy real-world sorting or fulfillment apps in an hour.
Simulations still cannot predict every real-world friction quirk (like gripper closure force on slippery wrappers), so builders still iterate controller thresholds against live camera feedback.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · HUMAN, FOUNDER & PHYSICAL AI LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Physical AI Finally Escaped the Integration Tax
castor.subtitleHtml: How folding Gemini Robotics ER 2 spatial reasoning into a $1.50/$7.50 generalist model changes hardware startups.
paragraphsHtml: In software, going from an idea to a working prototype takes an afternoon. In robotics, the gap between buying a 6-axis arm and picking up a pen off a desk has historically stretched into weeks of serial-bus drivers, depth-camera extrinsic calibration, URDF debugging, and standalone physics simulators.

On November 17, 2026, Google DeepMind’s Alex Gruenstein and Gabe Cohen attacked both halves of that bottleneck at once. On the model side, Gemini 4 Hydrogen absorbs the spatial and embodied capabilities of specialized Gemini Robotics ER 2 models—outperforming ER 2 on the public ERQA benchmark (multi-view correspondence and 3D trajectory reasoning) and scoring 58 on Artificial Analysis Robotics 0.1 across eight real 6-axis tabletop tasks.

On the tooling side, the new Robotics plugin for Google Antigravity turns the IDE into a unified Real-to-Sim-to-Real workbench. Plug in an I2RT YAM, budget SO-ARM101, or industrial FR3 Duo over USB, and Antigravity installs drivers, discovers depth cameras, calibrates kinematics, and verifies safe motion in roughly 10 minutes.

Because Hydrogen also writes full-stack web apps at $1.50 per 1M input tokens and $7.50 per 1M output tokens, one builder can now construct an online soap storefront and wire live order webhooks straight into dual YAM Pro arms—turning physical fulfillment into a single continuous codebase.

pullquote.quoteHtml: When embodied 3D reasoning lives inside the same fast model that writes your web storefront and renders your MuJoCo simulation, robotics stops being a separate engineering silo.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · REAL-TO-SIM-TO-REAL & WORKBENCH LENS
pollux.titleHtml: Inside the Four Antigravity Robotics Skills & MuJoCo Vibe Sim
pollux.subtitleHtml: How Robot bring-up, embedded MuJoCo auditing, and closed-loop camera control share one context window.
paragraphsHtml: Installing the plugin takes two clicks inside Google Antigravity: open Customizations and search for Robotics on the Build With Google shelf. Once enabled, four skill suites operate on your workspace: Robot bring-up, MuJoCo in Antigravity, Perception and control, and Application building.

In the "vibe sim" stage, you do not hand-craft MJCF XML files from scratch. Hydrogen generates and audits interactive MuJoCo assets directly from product information links, whiteboard sketches, or workspace photos—letting you adjust shapes, friction, and target positions in natural language and verify reaching/grasping before energizing real servos.

Once validated in simulation, the same controller deploys onto the calibrated arm via USB. As real-world edge cases appear—such as tuning gripper closure force on a snack wrapper or handling moving conveyor timing—you refine parameters conversationally while inspecting live depth-camera frames.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Always Run Bring-Up Safe Motion Checks First
builderRules.detailHtml: Start every hardware session with the Robot bring-up skill so joint limits, workspace collision bounds, and camera extrinsics are verified before closed-loop grasping.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Validate Edge Cases in MuJoCo Before Physical Runs
builderRules.detailHtml: Use MuJoCo asset auditing inside Antigravity to test conveyor speed variations and object clearances in simulation first, saving hardware wear.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Tune Real-World Grippers Iteratively on Live Frames
builderRules.detailHtml: Expect to follow sim validation with brief natural-language controller adjustments for real-world gripper closure pressure and lighting glare.

tejat.plainStandfirst: For years, personal AI assistants drafted polite emails and left you to sit on hold, log into utility portals, and type credit card numbers yourself. On November 17, 2026, Google flipped the toggle from passive chat to autonomous execution across six countries—and brought Google Wallet to iOS.
tejat.headlineHtml: Stop Copying Bills Into Chat. Gemini Now Runs Tasks End-to-End.
tejat.standfirstHtml: For years, personal AI assistants drafted polite emails and left you to sit on hold, log into utility portals, and type credit card numbers yourself. On November 17, 2026, Google flipped the toggle from passive chat to autonomous execution across six countries—and brought Google Wallet to iOS.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Tasks in Gemini (powered by Gemini 4 Hydrogen) rolled out free across the U.S., Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India—paired with U.S. Google Wallet on iOS and global Temporary Threads in Search AI Mode.
Flip Chat to Task, text via RCS, or forward emails to let Gemini place simultaneous phone calls, audit utility portals via Password Manager, and check out via AP2 with upfront hard spending caps.

Automated calling excludes 5 U.S. states (IN, LA, MN, MT, NE), tap-to-pay is absent on iOS Google Wallet, and strict anti-bot websites still require Gemini to hand the final checkout click back to you.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · CONSUMER, COMMERCE & TRUST LENS
castor.titleHtml: When Your Assistant Waits on Hold and Reads Your Electric Meter
castor.subtitleHtml: How Tasks in Gemini pairs AP2 tokenized spending caps with hardware-isolated microVMs.
paragraphsHtml: On November 17, 2026, VP Josh Woodward laid out the real daily friction Tasks in Gemini was built to erase: calling multiple car dealerships at once and sitting through hold music to snag a Friday service slot, digging through PDF statements and a utility portal (via Google Password Manager) to discover why a heat pump spiked an electric bill to $389 at 4:00 PM, and forwarding school emails so calendar invites catch schedule conflicts automatically.

Equally consequential is how users reach it. Instead of forcing everyone back into one app tab, Google opened three entry ramps in the U.S.: flipping the Gemini home-screen toggle from Chat to Task, texting via RCS on Android or iOS (including snapping a photo of an empty cereal box to add it to Instacart), or forwarding emails directly to <code>gemini@google.com</code>.

For purchases, Gemini adopts the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) with Google Pay (Mastercard, Visa, and American Express coming soon), preserving card rewards and purchase protections while enforcing user-set hard spending caps and pausing before clicking "Buy." Every receipt and tracking card flows into Google Wallet—which launched on iOS across the U.S. the exact same day.

And for moments when you want zero personalization or saved history, Google simultaneously launched Temporary Threads in AI Mode in Search globally across desktop and mobile browsers—detaching sessions completely from your Google Account.

pullquote.quoteHtml: For decades, websites blocked bots indiscriminately because most were malicious. Personal assistants force the web to build verifiable, user-authorized trust boundaries.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Can Gemini share my payment card or make a purchase without asking?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: No. Gemini runs in an isolated per-account virtual machine, refuses to share private account/payment details during calls unless instructed, enforces upfront spending caps via AP2, and pauses for confirmation before clicking Buy.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: What does Google Wallet on iOS support at launch?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: It digitizes loyalty cards and gym passes, manages Google Pay checkout cards, and serves as the unified hub for agentic purchase receipts and delivery tracking—though tap-to-pay is not supported on iOS.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Will businesses know when Gemini is calling on a customer’s behalf?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Yes. Google states Gemini discloses immediately on the call that it is an AI, and any business can opt out anytime via its Google Business Profile settings.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · AGENT COMPUTE ENGINE & COMMERCE PROTOCOLS
pollux.titleHtml: Five-Layer Defense-in-Depth, Connected Apps & UCP Readiness
pollux.subtitleHtml: How Google isolates consumer agent runs on Cloud microVMs—and what web and SaaS builders should integrate next.
paragraphsHtml: Running an autonomous browser agent across arbitrary websites, emails, and PDFs exposes the model to indirect prompt injections at internet scale. Google’s companion security overview by VP & Google Fellow Gautham Thambidorai details a five-layer architecture wrapping every Task: (1) Agent Compute Engine hardware-isolated cloud microVMs dedicated per user account, (2) Multi-stage prompt-injection filters and Google Safe Browsing link gating, (3) Policy Guardian vetting shell commands and outbound requests, (4) an Action Safety Agent gating sensitive operations, and (5) User Takeover browser handoffs for logins or sites that block automated sessions.

For developers and merchants, two integration surfaces matter most starting today: the Connected Apps Platform (already linking 60+ partners such as Instacart directly into Gemini Tasks) and the commerce stack bridging Shopping Graph, Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), and the upcoming Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP).

Instead of fighting bot-detection walls with brittle screen scrapers, participating apps expose structured actions and verifiable merchant capabilities so Gemini can populate carts, apply coupons, and hand off seamlessly to user-approved checkout.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Integrate via Connected Apps Rather Than DOM Scraping
builderRules.detailHtml: Apply to Google’s Connected Apps Platform so Gemini invokes typed actions directly and hands users clean pre-filled checkout screens.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Expose Clean Merchant Attributes for AP2 & UCP
builderRules.detailHtml: Ensure Shopping Graph product feeds include exact specs (wattage, finish, promo codes, stock) and prepare checkout flows for UCP tokenized settlement.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Respect Human Takeover at Auth & Final Purchase
builderRules.detailHtml: Mirror Google’s Action Safety Agent pattern in your own agents: isolate untrusted web browsing in microVMs and enforce hard caps plus explicit user confirmation.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · DEVELOPER WORKFLOW & COMMUNITY BUILDER LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Persistent Remote Hosts and Live PR Telemetry Change Daily Coding
castor.subtitleHtml: From closing your laptop mid-swarm to 1,048,576-particle WebGPU builds on Gemini 4 Carbon.
paragraphsHtml: For months, the biggest friction in agentic IDEs was physical: if you launched a multi-agent refactor or heavy test suite on your laptop, closing the lid froze your workspace. With Google Antigravity v2.33.0 (November 17, 2026), developers can connect directly to any remote 64-bit Linux machine via <code>~/.ssh/config</code>.

Antigravity automatically installs its remote server over OpenSSH so repositories, Git worktrees, agents, and terminals execute directly on the remote host—and keep working even after you close the Antigravity window.

At the same time, v2.33.0 closes the team-collaboration gap: GitHub Pull Request links inside chat and artifact cards now render as live status pills with hover cards alongside a dedicated Pull Requests section in Overview, while Business and Enterprise accounts unlock <code>/swarm</code> and partner UI plugin panels (Cloudflare, Grafana Cloud, SonarQube, incident.io, Better Stack, Tavily, Levels.fyi) under admin control.

Later the same afternoon on the official Google Blog, Google spotlighted five developers pushing Gemini 4 Carbon’s verification loops across heavy compute: Glitter Gal’s 52,000-wildflower CUDA/C++ meadow, Chubby’s 1,048,576-particle real-time WebGPU tidal flow, Andrew V’s stained-glass fracture game, Giyu_codes’s 14 interactive 3D public-data tools, and The Bugged Dev’s 92-instrument Parisian optics lab from a single reference image.

pullquote.quoteHtml: When agents persist on remote Linux servers while live GitHub PR telemetry sits right inside the Overview pane, the IDE stops acting like a local text editor and starts acting like mission control.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · HUMAN, ARCHITECT & EDGE AI LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Unified Multimodal Retrieval Matters Outside Hyperscale Data Centers
castor.subtitleHtml: How Gemma 4 and Gemini Embedding 2 research compressed four-modality search into an open edge footprint.
paragraphsHtml: Most real-world enterprise knowledge is messy and mixed-modal: a manufacturing defect report combines a technician’s voice memo, two smartphone photos, a 10-second video clip, and a PDF repair ticket. Historically, indexing those assets required stitching together incompatible embedding models—one for text, another for vision, another for audio—creating brittle retrieval pipelines that broke on cross-modal queries.

With EmbeddingGemma 2, Google expanded its open embedding series into native four-modality understanding—mapping text, images, audio, video, and arbitrary combinations into a single unified embedding space while compressing the backbone into a compact profile.

In the November 17 technical report (<code>arXiv:2610.37364</code>), the team revealed the recipe behind that compression: innovations drawn from Gemma 4 and Gemini Embedding 2, simplified per-layer embeddings, and a multi-stage training curriculum progressing systematically across modalities and retrieval objectives.
The result establishes a new Pareto frontier across unimodal, cross-modal, and mixed-modal benchmarks—outperforming both specialist single-modality models and open models 2x to 12x larger.

pullquote.quoteHtml: Beating models two to twelve times larger across text, image, audio, and video turns multimodal search from a cloud luxury into an on-device primitive.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Do I have to load audio and video encoders if my app only searches text and photos?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: No. EmbeddingGemma 2 explicitly supports selective modality encoder loading, so resource-constrained apps only keep the modality encoders they actively index in memory.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: How does EmbeddingGemma 2 help control storage and memory bills?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: It supports truncatable embedding dimensions and quantized weights, letting you dial down vector width while preserving strong cross-modal ranking quality.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: How does EmbeddingGemma 2 relate to Gemini Embedding 2?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: EmbeddingGemma 2 shares architectural innovations with Gemini Embedding 2 and Gemma 4—giving teams a unified open-weights sibling when data residency or offline on-device retrieval is required.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · TRAINING CURRICULUM & DEPLOYMENT KNOBS
pollux.titleHtml: Selective Encoders, Vision Token Budgets & Truncatable Vectors
pollux.subtitleHtml: Four architectural levers documented in arXiv:2610.37364 for fitting multimodal retrieval onto constrained hardware.
paragraphsHtml: According to <code>arXiv:2610.37364</code>, EmbeddingGemma 2’s performance rests on two foundational changes: simplified per-layer embeddings that keep the backbone compact, and a multi-stage curriculum with progressive modality and objective scheduling so text alignment never degrades when audio and video are introduced.

At inference time, builders gain four explicit efficiency knobs rather than a fixed black-box checkpoint: selective modality encoder loading (drop unused audio/video branches), adjustable vision token budgets (trade visual granularity for latency), truncatable embedding dimensions (compact storage), and quantized weights.

Combined with Google’s cloud <code>gemini-embedding-2</code> (now default for deprecated preview endpoints as of November 6) and Gen AI SDK v3.4.0 batch embeddings, teams can deploy identical mixed-modal search patterns from phones up to Vertex AI.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Load Only Active Modality Encoders on Edge
builderRules.detailHtml: Strip unused audio or video encoder weights at initialization on mobile or desktop clients to preserve memory headroom.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Tune Vision Token Budgets by Document Density
builderRules.detailHtml: Allocate higher vision token budgets for dense screenshots and engineering schematics, and lower budgets for coarse photo triage.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Truncate Dimensions Before Re-Indexing Large Corpora
builderRules.detailHtml: Benchmark truncated vector widths on your target mixed-modal eval set to maximize QPS and minimize RAM footprint in local vector stores.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google DeepMind research scientist Žiga Avsec explains how AlphaGenome (1M bp windows), AlphaGenome Atlas (AVI scores across all 9 billion single-letter DNA variants), and AlphaGenome 2’s cell-type specificity accelerate rare genetic disease discovery.

In Google DeepMind’s November 17 Ask a Scientist feature, genomics initiative lead Žiga Avsec breaks down the AlphaGenome stack: (1) AlphaGenome evaluates 1-million-base-pair DNA sequences to predict non-coding gene regulation effects, (2) AlphaGenome Atlas pre-computed all 9 billion possible single-letter substitutions across the 3-billion-base-pair human genome into instant AVI (AlphaGenome Variant Impact) scores, (3) Real-world clinical research validation—University of Exeter fellow Gareth Hawkes narrowed 1 billion variants to the top 1% to isolate 19 BMI-linked variant groups, while Broad Institute fellow Laura Covill resolved an unsolved rare neurodevelopmental disease case, and (4) AlphaGenome 2 advances beyond bulk tissue averages to cell-type-specific variant disruption and prediction confidence calibration.

alhena.headlineHtml: Your Agent Never Crashed—It Just Handed Over the Keys. Inside Agent Anomaly Detection.
alhena.standfirstHtml: When an autonomous agent leaks private records through an over-permissive tool or obeys an indirect prompt injection hidden inside an email, your server logs still return HTTP 200 OK. On November 16, 2026, Google published its hands-on deployment blueprint and 1,774-session independent benchmark audit for Agent Anomaly Detection alongside GTIG’s Q4 threat warning.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google Cloud published the hands-on deployment guide and 5-benchmark external audit for Agent Anomaly Detection (Private Preview), paired with GTIG’s Q4 2026 AI Threat Tracker and Google AI Threat Defense.

Security teams can flag out-of-scope tool misuse and OWASP #1 Goal Hijacks within ~5 minutes via Cloud Monitoring and Security Command Center without adding a single millisecond of latency to live user chats.
AAD is detective, not preventive—it needs ~300+ benign baseline sessions for peak recall (jumping from 33% to 99% on AgentDyn) and caught only 4 of 18 poisoned long-term memory attacks on ASB.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · HUMAN, FOUNDER & SECURITY LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why HTTP 200 OK Is No Longer Proof of Safety
castor.subtitleHtml: How Google’s asynchronous trace auditing and GTIG’s autonomous defense stack confront machine-speed agent abuse.
paragraphsHtml: Traditional software monitoring was built for a simpler failure model: when something broke, a process threw an exception, returned a 500 error, or spiked CPU. Autonomous AI agents fail silently while looking completely healthy. A customer support bot with an unguarded database lookup tool can accept an adversarial prompt, inspect an internal <code>payroll</code> table, and summarize employee salaries in fluent prose—all while reporting zero application errors.

That silent failure mode is why OWASP ranked Agent Goal Hijack first in its Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026). On November 16, 2026, Google Cloud engineers Achuth Narayan Rajagopal, Derek Luan, and Nakul Javali paired a step-by-step ADK deployment guide with something rare in AI security: an unmodified evaluation across 1,774 sessions spanning five external, non-Google-written security benchmarks (<code>AgentDojo</code>, <code>InjecAgent</code>, <code>Agent Security Bench</code>, <code>AgentDyn</code>, and <code>AgentHarm</code>).

Because deterministic Python state checks—not another LLM grader—verified whether money left an account or private data leaked, the results offer a grounded look at what asynchronous behavioral auditing can and cannot do. Out-of-band inspection flagged 87% of executed harmful instructions overall (reaching 99% on AgentDyn and 95%+ across 8 of 11 AgentDojo apps) while keeping benign office false alarms at 2% to 4% and adding 0 ms to live user response times.

Crucially, Google was equally candid about where AAD falls short: on Agent Security Bench, when malicious directives sat inside persistent long-term memory rather than immediate tool output, AAD caught only 4 of 18 attacks. Meanwhile, GTIG’s Q4 2026 Threat Tracker warned on the same day that attackers now run autonomous LLM loops to reverse-engineer software patches into working exploits—making layered prevention (Model Armor, Semantic Governance Policy, CodeMender, and Wiz) non-negotiable.

pullquote.quoteHtml: Security tools always look impressive on tests their own team wrote. Testing asynchronously across 1,774 external benchmark sessions proved 87% recall at zero latency—and exposed poisoned memory as the next frontier.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Does enabling Agent Anomaly Detection slow down streaming Gemini responses?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: No. Agent Anomaly Detection runs asynchronously out-of-band by reading OpenTelemetry traces and Cloud Logging events after execution, adding 0 ms of latency to live user responses while surfacing findings within roughly 5 minutes.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Can Agent Anomaly Detection block a malicious tool call before data leaves?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: No—it is a detective audit layer that emits AGENT_SESSION_ANOMALY findings to Security Command Center and Cloud Monitoring. To block calls inline, pair it with strict tool allowlists, Model Armor prompt/tool screening, and Semantic Governance Policy.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: What Google Cloud prerequisites are required to try it today?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: You need Private Preview approval on a billed Google Cloud project, ADK 1.2+ (2.0+ preferred), and both a Cloud Logging bucket and Observability dataset located in the same US or EU multi-region.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · ARCHITECTURE, OTEL INSTRUMENTATION & BLUEPRINT
pollux.titleHtml: Instrumenting ADK Telemetry, 5-Minute Delta Alerts & Hardened Tool Allowlists
pollux.subtitleHtml: How three OpenTelemetry environment variables unlock behavioral auditing across Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, and GKE.
paragraphsHtml: Agent Anomaly Detection discovers agents automatically through their OpenTelemetry spans—meaning an un-instrumented agent or one that has never handled a test message will not appear under Monitored agents. Setting three environment variables on your Agent Runtime deployment (<code>GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY</code>, <code>OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN</code>, and <code>OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT</code>) writes structured prompt and response events directly to Cloud Logging and Cloud Trace.

In the November 16 hands-on guide, individual probing turns inside a refund conversation each scored Medium severity, yet AAD aggregated the multi-turn escalation into a single High-severity Tool misuse session finding at 95% probability—complete with a 3-pane forensic view (Session severity, Conversation transcript, and Detector rationale recommending an explicit table allowlist on <code>fetch_records</code>).

For production alerting, wire Cloud Monitoring to the <code>Detected events</code> metric with a 5-minute rolling window and <code>delta</code> aggregator above 0, alongside a metric-absence policy on <code>Monitored agents</code> so you immediately notice if a deployment accidentally strips telemetry flags.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Pair Async Audit with Pre-Call Allowlists
builderRules.detailHtml: Never rely solely on post-execution detection for sensitive schemas; validate table names, customer IDs, and outbound domains deterministically inside tool wrappers.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Calibrate with 300+ Benign Baseline Sessions
builderRules.detailHtml: Run staging or replay traffic past 300 benign sessions before gating production releases—recall on AgentDyn jumped from 33% at 220 runs to 99% at 360 runs.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Defend Persistent Memory Separately
builderRules.detailHtml: Because AAD caught only 4 of 18 poisoned-memory sessions on ASB, sign long-term memory writes with provenance metadata and validate recall payloads before prompt injection.

pollux.codeCaptionHtml: ADK OPENTELEMETRY INSTRUMENTATION & HARDENED TOOL ALLOWLIST

workbench.dekHtml: Compare how OTel async auditing, Model Armor, and Semantic Governance Policy behave across Google’s Nov 16 test scenarios, or open the interactive lab.

verdict.titleHtml: Gemini’s Bottom Line: Instrument Telemetry First, Then Layer Prevention
verdict.subtitleHtml: Zero-latency behavioral auditing belongs on every production ADK agent—so long as teams treat it as one ring of defense-in-depth.
paragraphsHtml: Deploy immediately in staging & Private Preview if: your ADK agents read external emails, web pages, or multi-table databases where a silent HTTP 200 breach would cost customer trust or regulatory standing.

Do not stop at detection: Google’s own benchmark honesty proves that asynchronous auditing must sit behind deterministic tool allowlists, Model Armor input filtering, Semantic Governance Policy, and signed memory provenance.
